analyst_view.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 pts) and Rennes (8th, 16 pts), one point apart. Rennes have won one of their last six in all competitions, conceded 21 league goals, and their chairman put Franck Haise under public pressure on 17 November, with Blas, Nordin and Merlin reportedly pushed out of the squad (Maxifoot, Foot01, GFFN). The numbers count Rennes' top scorer Esteban Lepaul (7 goals in 7 games, ankle sprain) as out; he was close to a return before the break and an earlier report said he is set to play here, but I could not re-confirm it. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) are a stubborn defensive side who won 2-0 at Le Havre last time; Katseris, Fadiga, Bamba and Ibrahima Baldé are in the numbers' missing list. Marc Bollengier referees (4.1 cards per game, already counted); no match preview was out yet, so the view leans on club and league news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and cut Rennes' by about 20% for Lepaul. Sports Mole said on 8 November he might return soon and after the two-week break a comeback is plausible (one earlier report said he is set to play), so I give back part of that, to about 2.6. Lorient's tight defence (four conceded in six) is already counted and keeps this modest.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Rennes slightly ahead (5.1 v 4.3). Haise has switched between a back three with wing-backs and a 4-3-3, and Lorient sit deep at home, which the numbers already reflect; I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, including Bollengier's slightly strict record (+6% already counted). A derby between neighbours with Rennes under pressure has some edge, but the brief carries no derby flag and both sides' recent card counts are normal, so I stay at about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots, already up for Rennes' busy shooting (85 in six) and down for Lorient's low volume. A Lepaul return would change who finishes the chances more than how many Rennes create, so I stay at about 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Lepaul, if he plays, is Rennes' most accurate finisher, so I go slightly up to about 9.3; Lorient's low recent output on target (14 in six) is already in the numbers.
